title: 10 Things to Do in Mirleft, Morocco
description: Wild beaches, surf, sunsets over red cliffs and slow souk mornings — our local guide to the best things to do in Mirleft on Morocco's Atlantic coast.

body.p: Mirleft is a small town on Morocco's southern Atlantic coast, between Tiznit and Sidi Ifni. It has no big hotels, no crowds and no rush — just a string of wild beaches, a friendly little centre and some of the best sunsets in the country. Here is how our guests like to spend their days.

Tamelalt Beach is about 50 metres from [our villas](/villas), with golden sand dunes just behind it. Go early in the morning when the sand is cool and the beach is almost empty, or late afternoon when the light turns gold.

body.h2: 2. Watch the sunset from a rooftop

body.p: The sun sets straight into the Atlantic here. Our rooftop conservatory and terraces are the best seats in the house — bring a mint tea or a cold drink and stay until the stars come out.

Mirleft's beaches pick up consistent Atlantic swell and are far quieter than the famous breaks further north. Local surf schools offer lessons and board rental for every level — read our [surfing guide](/journal/surfing-in-mirleft) for tips.

body.h2: 4. Explore the coves and beaches along the coast

body.p: The coastline around Mirleft is a series of sheltered coves framed by rocky headlands. Each beach has its own character, from long open sand to small hidden bays. A car or bicycle makes it easy to hop between them.
A short drive south towards Sidi Ifni, Legzira Beach is known for its dramatic red sandstone cliffs and arch. Time your visit for low tide and late afternoon light.
Quad bike and horse riding excursions along the dunes and beach can be arranged through trusted local operators. Ask us and we'll set it up.
Mirleft's centre is small and relaxed: a few streets of cafés, grocers, craft shops and a weekly souk. It's the perfect place to pick up fresh bread, fruit and spices for the villa kitchen.
The catch comes in daily. Try it at Ocean Dunes House, our on-site restaurant, or grill your own on the villa BBQ. See our [dining page](/dining) for menus and hours.
The resort has a tennis court and bicycles to rent — a lovely way to explore the coast road at your own pace.
Honestly, this is what Mirleft does best. A private pool, a good book and the sound of the ocean. When you're ready, [check availability](/booking) for your dates.

title: How to Get from Agadir to Mirleft
description: Flying into Agadir? Here's how to get to Mirleft by car, taxi or private transfer — distances, travel times and practical tips for the drive south.

body.p: Most guests fly into Agadir Al-Massira Airport (AGA), the closest international airport to Mirleft. From there it's a scenic drive south along the Atlantic. Guelmim Airport is the other option, a little further away.

Renting a car at the airport gives you the most freedom to explore the coast. Head south on the N1 towards Tiznit, then follow the coast road to Mirleft. The roads are paved and well maintained — a standard car is fine, no 4x4 needed. Allow around two hours.
Tips: drive in daylight on your first trip, keep some small change for roadside cafés, and download offline maps before you set off.

The easiest option after a long flight. We can arrange a paid private transfer that meets you at arrivals and brings you straight to the villa. Just mention it in your [booking request](/booking) or [message us on WhatsApp](/contact).
Shared grand taxis and buses run from Agadir to Tiznit, where you can change for Mirleft. It's the cheapest route but takes longer and needs a bit of patience with connections.

We're at Route d'Aglou in Tamelalt, inside the Club Evasion resort, about 50 metres from the beach. Check-in is from 15:00; if you're arriving late, let us know and we'll be ready for you. See the [location page](/location) for the map and GPS coordinates.

title: Surfing in Mirleft: A Beginner-Friendly Guide
description: Why Mirleft is one of Morocco's best-kept surf secrets — when to go, what to expect, lessons for beginners and where to stay near the waves.

body.p: Morocco's surf reputation was built further north, around Taghazout. Mirleft offers the same Atlantic swell with a fraction of the crowds — which makes it a brilliant place to learn, or to surf uncrowded peaks if you already ride.

Autumn through spring brings the most consistent swell to this coast, with the biggest days in winter. Summer is usually smaller and gentler — ideal for beginners and families. The water is cool year-round, so bring or rent a wetsuit.

Local surf schools offer group and private lessons with boards and wetsuits included. Instructors know which beach will be working on the day, depending on tide and wind. We're happy to recommend and book a school for you.
Atlantic beaches can have strong currents. Surf with a guide until you know the spots, respect the locals, and never paddle out alone on bigger days.

There's nothing better than rinsing off in your own pool and watching the evening sets roll in from the terrace. Our [two villas](/villas) are a short walk from Tamelalt Beach — [check availability](/booking) for your surf trip.

title: The Best Time to Visit Mirleft
description: Mirleft enjoys mild weather all year. Here's what each season brings — sun, swell, crowds and prices — so you can pick the perfect time for your stay.

body.p: Thanks to the Atlantic, Mirleft avoids the extreme heat of inland Morocco. Days are warm and bright for most of the year, and evenings can be cool — pack a light jumper whatever the season.
Our favourite season: warm sunny days, green hillsides, good surf and quiet beaches. Perfect for couples and anyone who wants to explore the coast.
The liveliest months, popular with families and Moroccan holidaymakers. The ocean breeze keeps temperatures comfortable and the sea is at its calmest. Book early — villas fill up fast.
Still warm, with the swell returning and the summer crowds gone. Great for surfers and long, lazy beach days.
Mild and sunny compared with Europe, which makes Mirleft a popular winter escape. Nights are cooler, the surf is at its biggest, and the sunsets are spectacular.

Whatever the season, both villas have a private pool, full kitchen and terraces facing the ocean. Cancellation is free and there's no prepayment — [check your dates](/booking) or [ask us anything](/contact).
